name: dcore
description: Universal, fail-closed Claude Code skill set for framing, specifying, planning, reviewing, QA, debugging, security review and release readiness — composable via deterministic handoff, installable by clone, no certification/credentials/network required.

modules.purpose: turn a raw request into a framed problem (objective, stakeholders, risks, open questions)
turn a problem into a structured specification
turn a feature/request into an implementation plan
produce a structured review of code or a real unified diff (diff mode reviews added lines only, with file:line)

test plan scaffold from text; --discover generates executable scenarios from a live page; --plan executes a test plan in a real browser; --scenarios executes functional scenarios across browser/API/command/verify steps with per-step evidence (negative/boundary cases: HELD or VIOLATED, violations become defect candidates; --only selects a subset); both write the Detailed Test Report, Detailed Defect Report and Test Case Register (PDF + JSON + Markdown)
turn a defect report into hypotheses, evidence to collect, likely root causes and next steps
threat-model a change (assets, surface, STRIDE-style checks, findings, residual risk); with --repo also scan the working tree (CONFIRMED / SUSPICIOUS / THEORETICAL)
turn a feature/spec/change into a deterministic documentation scaffold (known vs UNKNOWN, no invented APIs)

fail-closed release readiness: a go/no-go checklist from text, or with --repo EXECUTE the gates (tree, upstream, tests, secrets, version, docs) => READY/BLOCKED/NOT_AUTHORIZED/FAILED/VERIFIED; push/deploy only with approval
run the common frame -> spec -> plan -> qa path in one call, composing via deterministic handoff
given a change + a repo, find literal references and classify DIRECT_EVIDENCE / LIKELY_AFFECTED / POSSIBLY_AFFECTED / UNKNOWN (never a dependency graph)

read-only repository intelligence (project type, languages, frameworks, commands, entry points, CI, integrations, config; secret files by name only); --app: passive application discovery (deterministic app map + candidate scenarios); --coverage: DISCOVERED/TESTED lifecycle after a run
implement the smallest coherent change following repository conventions, then verify with dcore-run (Claude edits files with its own tools)
add focused tests (regression, edge cases) that follow the repository test conventions, then run them
run one repository-local command (tests/lint/typecheck/build) with timeout, redacted output, failure classification; destructive commands need approval
execute real HTTP requests with status/header/body/JSON-path/schema/latency assertions; writes to non-local hosts need approval; secrets from env only, redacted
drive a real Chromium-family browser (CDP, no dependencies): navigate, click, fill, assert, screenshot, console/network errors, a11y heuristics, timing; BLOCKED when no browser exists
status/diff/log/branches/show; commit and push only with explicit approval; push verified against the remote; never force-push or rewrite history
verify a deployed environment: health endpoints, expected page/text, latency, optional browser smoke => VERIFIED/FAILED/BLOCKED; never auto-rollback
project retrospective scaffold

execution_layer.subprocess: dcore-run (the one requested command), dcore-git (git), dcore-browse (the local browser), dcore-release (git + test command)
execution_layer.network: only dcore-api / dcore-browse / dcore-verify, only to the URL the user gives; never in reasoning modules
execution_layer.credentials: only from environment variables the user names (valueEnv / --auth-env); always redacted from evidence
execution_layer.approvals: git-commit, git-push, deploy, release, production, db-destructive, delete, external-write, credential, account, destructive-command — per invocation via --approve
